rumors.text: A wounded treasure hunter came down from the cliffs last month, muttering about a drowned sword and a map torn in two.
The well-keeper swears the old well hums at night, as if something below were breathing.
Travellers say a Core Formation cultivator was struck down by his tribulation on the Azure Peak. Prepare well before you try.
Herb pickers say that if you wander the Misty Forest long enough, the mist parts on a valley no map shows.
They say something old and green keeps that hidden valley, and it only speaks to those who have walked the forest a long while.
Mist wolves hunt in packs this season; the foresters never go in alone.
Disciples of the peak whisper that on windless nights the cliffs ring with sword-song from a tomb no one has entered.
Do not follow the green lanterns in the marsh, friend, unless you wish to meet whoever lit them.
The old ferrymen say the Drowned Yin Palace rises with the cold tide, once in a great while, and those who enter rarely agree on what they saw.
The beast clans of the ridge keep their own laws; hunters who ignore them do not come home.
A patriarch is said to have died upright on a ridge crag, the lightning still circling his seat for any who dare to sit.
The back rooms of the market trade in things the guild would rather not price; ask quietly, and bring stones.
The grandmothers say the founder of Qingshi was no farmer, and that his kindness is still remembered by whoever kneels at the well.
An immortal's legacy waits in every great mountain, they say, but it tests the heart before it tests the blade.
Old hands say the secret realms open by the calendar of heaven, not of men; the ones who keep count are the ones who get in.
